title: Social force model for pedestrian dynamics
finding: Social-force motion model; not a clearance-time forecasting benchmark.
limitation: No support for the draft demographic coefficients.

authors: Moussaid, Mehdi and Perozo, Niriaska and Garnier, Simon and Helbing, Dirk and Theraulaz, Guy
title: The Walking Behaviour of Pedestrian Social Groups and Its Impact on Crowd Dynamics
finding: Observed formations motivate persistent group features.
limitation: Social ties cannot be inferred from proximity alone; natural walking differs from evacuation.

authors: Bode, Nikolai W. F. and Holl, Stefan and Mehner, Wolfgang and Seyfried, Armin
title: Disentangling the Impact of Social Groups on Response Times and Movement Dynamics in Evacuations
finding: Reported delay differences mainly in response and approach stages, not directly before exits.
limitation: Do not assume a universal bottleneck friction penalty. Supplementary data are advertised, not audited here.

authors: von Kruchten, Cornelia and Schadschneider, Andreas
title: Empirical study on social groups in pedestrian evacuation dynamics
evidence_level: publisher indexed abstract; full page blocked
finding: Empirical group-configuration study relevant to group descriptors.
limitation: Full methods and numerical conclusions not verified.

authors: Xie, Wei and Lee, Eric Wai Ming and Li, Tao and Shi, Meng and Cao, Ruifeng and Zhang, Yuchun
title: A study of group effects in pedestrian crowd evacuation: Experiments, modelling and simulation
finding: Calibrated social-force group model; effects depend on geometry and behaviour.
limitation: Not evidence that group membership always increases clearance time.

authors: Fu, Libi and Shi, Qingxin and Qin, Huigui and Zhang, Ying and Shi, Yongqian
title: Analysis of movement behavior of pedestrian social groups through a bottleneck
evidence_level: publisher indexed preview; full page blocked
finding: Controlled bottleneck experiment examines group size, width, and splitting/rejoining.
limitation: Raw data and detailed analysis not inspected.

authors: Hu, Yanghui and Zhang, Jun and Song, Weiguo and Bode, Nikolai W. F.
title: Social groups barely change the speed-density relationship in unidirectional pedestrian flow, but affect operational behaviours
finding: Group differences were more evident in operational behaviours than the speed-density relationship.
limitation: Normal unidirectional flow; incremental forecasting value remains to be tested.

authors: Kuligowski, Erica D. and Peacock, Richard D. and Wiess, Emily and Hoskins, Bryan
title: Stair evacuation of older adults and people with mobility impairments
finding: Observed evacuation mobility variation supports studying measured movement.
limitation: Stair evidence cannot calibrate flat-corridor coefficients without justification.

authors: Feliciani, Claudio and Murakami, Hisashi and Shimura, Kenichiro and Nishinari, Katsuhiro
title: Efficiently informing crowds - Experiments and simulations on route choice and decision making in pedestrian crowds with wheelchair users
evidence_level: author bibliography and publisher indexed preview
finding: Studies information, route choice and wheelchair-inclusive evacuation.
limitation: Do not transfer its results to fixed footprint multipliers; full methods not inspected.

authors: Li, Hongliu and Zhang, Jun and Xia, Long and Yang, Libing and Song, Weiguo and Yuen, Kwok Kit Richard
title: Characteristic time in highly motivated movements of children and adults through bottlenecks
finding: Compares child and adult bottleneck motion and timing.
limitation: Not validation of appearance-based age labels or a fixed parental protective bubble.

authors: Redmon, Joseph and Divvala, Santosh and Girshick, Ross and Farhadi, Ali
title: You Only Look Once: Unified, Real-Time Object Detection

authors: Wojke, Nicolai and Bewley, Alex and Paulus, Dietrich
title: Simple Online and Realtime Tracking with a Deep Association Metric
limitation: Tracking accuracy does not establish companion identity.

authors: Li, Yuhong and Zhang, Xiaofan and Chen, Deming
title: CSRNet: Dilated Convolutional Neural Networks for Understanding the Highly Congested Scenes
limitation: Correct first-author attribution is Li, not Zhang; not a clearance predictor.

authors: Alqahtani, Fahad K. and Sherif, Mohamed and Ghanem, Amr and Abdelhafeez, Mostafa
title: Inclusive crowd evacuation modeling under heterogeneous mobility constraints
evidence_level: publisher indexed PDF and PMC indexed sections
finding: Existing inclusive social-force simulation directly overlaps broad mobility-aware modelling claims.
limitation: Calibration and internal consistency require deeper appraisal; cannot treat all reported settings as validated constants.

authors: Smania Testa, Estevao and Raupp Musse, Soraia
title: Predicting and Optimizing Crowd Evacuations: An Explainable AI Approach
finding: Simulation-trained ANN predicts evacuation quantities and uses explainability for design.
limitation: Different from online remaining-time prediction; data are on request, not audited as downloadable.

authors: Berggold, P. and Borrmann, A. and Nousias, S.
title: Graph neural networks for building evacuation prediction: integrating real-time pedestrian flow simulation into BIM workflows
finding: Graph-based temporal density-class prediction is an existing evacuation surrogate.
limitation: Not a direct group-conditioned remaining-clearance baseline; node classification target differs.

authors: Hu, Yanghui and Bode, Nikolai W. F.
title: A systematic review and meta-analysis on the effect social groups have on the egress times of pedestrian crowds
finding: Six comparable studies; aggregated evidence insufficient to reject no group effect.
limitation: Online year is used; final issue metadata not checked. Supports cautious hypotheses and independent samples.

authors: Choubey, Nipun and Verma, Ashish and Chakraborty, Anirban
title: An unsupervised group detection method for understanding group dynamics in crowds
finding: Adaptive rankSBP group association is prior art beyond simple velocity matching.
limitation: Full implementation not inspected; prefer publisher DOI over conflicting secondary citation.
